Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) Support access / break-glass: we need a concrete description of: who can trigger break-glass, what approvals are required, how the event is logged, and what the notification chain looks like. Is there a tamper-evident audit trail you can provide?
2) RBAC: can you share role definitions and example least-privilege mappings (admin, support, read-only analytics, model ops)? We want to see how identity maps to roles (SCIM / OIDC) and whether we can enforce just-in-time elevation.
3) Data residency & retention: production must be EU-only for FinTrust. We also have a strict 90-day retention policy for PII by default; does Redwood support per-tenant retention windows and deletion APIs?
4) Logs & monitoring: retention windows for request/response logs, and whether logs contain PII or pseudonymized IDs. Also interested in whether Redwood supports exporting audit logs to our Splunk instance.

If you can answer those high level, we can decide whether to proceed to the technical session. Looping in Sonia from our legal/compliance for any contractual notes.

—
Alex Johnson

Alex / Sonia — thanks for the questions. Answers below at a high level; we can deep-dive on any bullet during the technical session.

1) Support access / break-glass
- Who: break-glass can be initiated by senior SRE or Support Lead and requires a two-person approval (engineer + manager) for one-off emergency access.
- Approvals: implemented via our ticketing flow (linked to PagerDuty and internal change control). Emergency approval is recorded and pinned to the access event.
- Audit trail: all break-glass events are logged with user, timestamp, justification, and session recording reference. Logs are tamper-evident (write-once append-only storage) and checksums are verified nightly.
- Notifications: automated email + webhook notifications to customer's security inbox and the internal security Slack channel.

2) RBAC & identity
- Roles: we provide pre-built role templates (admin, support, read-only analytics, model-ops) which you can customize per-tenant.
- Identity: SCIM provisioning and OIDC support for SSO; support for just-in-time elevation via short-lived signed tokens (can be gated to require approval workflows).

3) Data residency & retention
- Residency: we support per-tenant region pinning. For EU-only production, we can pin storage and inference to EU regions; metadata minimal replication to control plane in US can be disabled.
- Retention: per-tenant retention windows are supported and enforceable via our deletion APIs. We can configure default 90-day PII retention and provide deletion receipts.

4) Logs & monitoring
- Request/response logs: by default we store request metadata and token-level billing traces. Full request/response capture is optional and can be disabled or pseudonymized.
- Export: we support pushing audit logs to customer Splunk/ELK via secure connectors and S3 exports. Retention windows are configurable; we can retain audit logs for 1 year or longer as required.

Attachments: I also attached a short "support-access-process.pdf" that outlines the operational flow and sample audit record.

Next steps:
- Ethan, can you propose two slots today or tomorrow for a 45-min technical deep-dive focused on RBAC and break-glass?
- Alex/Sonia, if you can confirm EU-only residency and the 90-day PII retention requirement we'll include that in the mutual action plan.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
